briefs.title: Relief Building on Both Fronts: MI Tax Fight Heats Up Ahead of November as DEA's Schedule III Hearing Nears the Finish Line
briefs.top: In Michigan, bipartisan momentum against the 24% wholesale tax is building fast heading into the governor's race, while a Michigan-rooted brand just proved operators can still scale. Nationally, the DEA's Schedule III rescheduling hearing is entering its final stretch and psychedelics are notching real regulatory wins, giving operators genuine reasons for optimism this fall.
briefs.label: Morning Brief

local.text: The GOP's nominee for governor is now promising to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale cannabis tax if elected in November, joining a Democratic primary rival who made the same pledge earlier this year — turning tax relief into a genuine bipartisan campaign issue operators can rally behind.

MiCIA's original constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax is now heading to trial in September, giving operators their first real day in court after a new backup lawsuit was also filed against the Treasury — a concrete legal pathway to relief after months of layoffs and closures.

A fresh repeal bill, HB 6224, cleared committee referral this month and joins a companion Senate measure that already has three Democratic cosponsors — signaling the repeal push now has real legislative legs on both sides of the aisle.

Michigan-rooted multistate operator JARS Cannabis just struck a deal to acquire Arizona's Sonoran Roots, a move that would give the combined company 27 dispensaries and make it Arizona's largest retail cannabis network — proof a Michigan brand can still expand aggressively even amid the state's tax squeeze.

Michigan flower hit a record-low average retail price of $58 an ounce in June, down from $63 a year ago — rock-bottom prices are squeezing margins, but they're also fueling the kind of consumer demand and volume that keeps the country's second-largest legal market moving while relief efforts play out.

national.text: The DEA is now holding its hearing on moving marijuana fully from Schedule I to Schedule III, the final step after April's move to reschedule state-licensed medical cannabis, with the full hearing transcript already released and the presiding judge preparing his formal recommendation.

Curaleaf formally commenced its takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on Aug. 18, offering a 45% premium and pitching a combined company spanning 17 countries — a sign consolidation and U.S.-market access are back at the top of the industry's agenda.

The FDA granted Compass Pathways a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for its psilocybin therapy COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, with the company targeting commercial launch-readiness by the end of 2026 — putting the first classic psychedelic on a real path to approval.

Glass House Brands rang the New York Stock Exchange closing bell this week, roughly two months after its shares began trading under ticker GLAS — another sign mainstream capital markets are opening up to plant-touching operators.

The FDA's finalized psychedelics guidance signals the agency is receptive to helping companies succeed, following a Trump executive order urging health agencies to build an established approval path for psilocybin, MDMA and even ibogaine — momentum that extends well beyond Compass into the wider functional-mushroom and mental-health space.
